bugs.explanation: A `<div class="navigation">` communicates nothing to assistive technologies. Use the semantic `<nav>` element for navigation landmark regions. Screen readers announce it as navigation and allow users to jump to it directly.

Use the `<main>` landmark element instead of `<div id="main-content">` for the primary content area. Screen readers allow users to skip directly to `<main>` and it maps to the ARIA `main` landmark role.

title: article vs section
code:
My Blog Post

This post is about...

Author: Alice. Posted: 2024-01-01.

bugs.fix:
My Blog Post

This post is about...

Author: Alice. Posted: Jan 1, 2024.
bugs.explanation: Blog posts, news articles, and self-contained content should use `<article>`, not `<section>`. `<article>` signals that the content is independently distributable (e.g., via RSS). Also wrap publication metadata in `<footer>` and use `<time>` for dates.

Use `<aside>` for content that is tangentially related to the surrounding content (sidebars, pull quotes, related links). `<aside>` maps to the ARIA `complementary` landmark, allowing screen reader navigation to skip or jump to it.
Use semantic `<header>` and `<footer>` elements instead of `<div>` with classes. They map to `banner` and `contentinfo` ARIA landmarks respectively, enabling screen reader landmark navigation.

Use `<address>` for contact information related to the nearest `<article>` or `<body>`. It should contain the actual contact info (not just a label). Email addresses should be wrapped in `<a href="mailto:...">` for interactivity.

title: figure and figcaption
code: Figure 1: Sales over time

bugs.explanation: Use `<figure>` and `<figcaption>` to associate an image with its caption. This creates a semantic relationship that screen readers can convey. `<figcaption>` should complement (not duplicate) the alt text.

title: details and summary
code: Click Settings then Reset.

bugs.fix:
FAQ: How do I reset?

Click Settings then Reset.
bugs.explanation: For disclosure widgets (show/hide content), the native `<details>`/`<summary>` pattern is simpler than a custom button+div approach. It works without JavaScript, is keyboard accessible, and announces state to screen readers automatically.

The native `<dialog>` element provides built-in dialog semantics, focus management, and a `showModal()` API that traps focus correctly. It's better than a `<div role="dialog">` which requires significant JavaScript to implement the same behavior.

Use the semantic `<progress>` element for task completion or `<meter>` for a value within a known range. They render native OS progress bars and are announced correctly by screen readers, unlike plain text percentages.

Wrap date and time strings in `<time datetime="...">`. The `datetime` attribute provides a machine-readable format that search engines, calendar apps, and assistive technologies can parse, even if the human-readable text is different.

title: mark for Highlighted Text
code: Search result: the word JavaScript was found

bugs.explanation: Use `<mark>` to highlight text that is relevant in context (search results, current search terms). It conveys semantic meaning and is announced by some screen readers. `<span class="highlight">` only provides visual styling with no semantic meaning.

bugs.fix: CSS makes the page look great.
bugs.explanation: Wrap abbreviations in `<abbr title="full form">` on first use. This helps readers who may not know the abbreviation, and assistive technologies can expose the full form. The `title` attribute provides the expansion.

title: cite for Works
code: As said in "The Art of Clean Code":

bugs.fix: As said in The Art of Clean Code:
bugs.explanation: Use `<cite>` to semantically mark the title of a creative work (books, films, articles). It conveys that the enclosed text is a reference to a work, not just italicized text.

title: blockquote With cite
code: "The best code is no code at all." — Jeff Atwood

bugs.fix:
The best code is no code at all.

— Jeff Atwood
bugs.explanation: Use `<blockquote>` for block-level quotations, with an optional `cite` attribute pointing to the source. The attribution should go inside `<footer>` with the name wrapped in `<cite>`.

title: dl dt dd for Definition Lists
code:
• HTTP: HyperText Transfer Protocol
  • HTML: HyperText Markup Language

bugs.explanation: For term-definition pairs, use `<dl>` (description list) with `<dt>` (term) and `<dd>` (definition). A `<ul>` with concatenated text doesn't convey the term/definition relationship semantically.

bugs.fix:
<input type="text" name="zip" id="zip"
  pattern="[0-9]{5}" inputmode="numeric"
  placeholder="12345" autocomplete="postal-code">
bugs.explanation: For specific formats like zip codes, add `pattern` for validation, `inputmode="numeric"` to show a numeric keyboard on mobile, and `autocomplete` for browser autofill. These significantly improve the user experience.

bugs.fix:
<input type="text" name="browser" list="browsers">
<datalist id="browsers">
  <option value="Chrome">
  <option value="Firefox">
  <option value="Safari">
</datalist>
bugs.explanation: The `<datalist>` element provides a native autocomplete dropdown for text inputs without any JavaScript. Link the input to the datalist with `list` attribute matching the datalist's `id`.

`<output>` is the semantic element for displaying computed or reactive values. The `for` attribute links it to the input that drives the output, providing meaningful association for assistive technologies.

bugs.fix:
<search>
  <form action="/search">
    <input type="search" name="q" placeholder="Search..." aria-label="Search">
    <button type="submit">Search</button>
  </form>
</search>
bugs.explanation: The `<search>` element (new in HTML 2023 spec) provides a landmark role for search widgets. Wrap search forms in `<search>` so screen reader users can navigate directly to the search landmark. Also add `aria-label` to the input.
